items.title: Gemini task automation expands to 40+ apps, Samsung shows off two more Android XR glasses
items.excerpt: Google expanded Gemini's on-device task automation to over 40 apps across shopping, restaurant reservations, travel booking and event tickets, debuting on Samsung's new Galaxy Z foldables. The agentic assistant can read on-screen context and complete multi-step actions inside third-party apps without the user hopping between them.

items.title: Samsung's latest foldables gain a new way to keep tabs on AI
items.excerpt: One UI 9 on the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Fold 8 Ultra and Flip 8 introduces a central AI Assistant Activity dashboard, a single place to monitor the background AI automations that Gemini Intelligence performs on your behalf. It is Samsung's attempt to make on-device agentic AI transparent and controllable as assistants start acting autonomously.

items.title: Galaxy Watch 9, Watch Ultra 2 are here: Samsung's health partners bring soft comfort and more
items.excerpt: Samsung launched the Galaxy Watch 9 and rugged Watch Ultra 2 with new AI-driven health features including a personalized health coach, a Fitness Index, Vascular Load and expanded sleep and heart insights tied to its new AI Health Assistant. The wearables lean on upgraded internals for longer, more accurate on-body monitoring.

items.title: Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 review: the best Samsung watch ever created
items.excerpt: A hands-on review of Samsung's rugged flagship smartwatch finds its real-time AI health insights, improved tracking accuracy and returning Running Coach make it the strongest Galaxy watch to date. The verdict weighs how much of the AI coaching genuinely changes daily use versus adding noise.

items.title: I briefly tried Gemini Intelligence, and I'm still not sure who it's for
items.excerpt: A hands-on with Gemini Intelligence, the new on-device agentic layer debuting on Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8, questions whether the automated task-running and gen-UI widgets actually fit how people use their phones. It is an early, skeptical read on the first wave of always-on agent hardware experiences.
